subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What signed-skill trust model should OpenClaw enforce before SKILL.md content is loaded into runtime prompts or granted capabilities?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent answer depends on security-boundary choices around trust roots, publisher signatures, revocation, unsigned compatibility, and capability/profile policy.

options.title: Design integrated signed-skill enforcement
options.body: Specify trusted metadata, signature verification, lock/origin persistence, runtime checks, status surfaces, and unsigned capability restrictions before implementation.

options.title: Keep verification advisory-only for now
options.body: Continue exposing ClawHub trust cards and local provenance while leaving runtime loading permissive until the security model matures.

options.title: Defer enforcement to external policies
options.body: Rely on ClawHub packages, install policies, or third-party tools for signed-skill enforcement and keep core out of the runtime trust decision.

recommendation.title: Design integrated signed-skill enforcement
recommendation.body: Specify trusted metadata, signature verification, lock/origin persistence, runtime checks, status surfaces, and unsigned capability restrictions before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available routing signal from current skill/runtime line history and prior issue review, while Patrick-Erichsen and momothemage are adjacent implementation owners.
